CLASS 31 · PRESCHOOL AGES 4–5

Science, Nature & Discovery

Age 4–5 YearsClass 31 of 31Adventures 30 science gamesSubjects Plants · animals · weather · light · sound

Explore plants, animals, weather, habitats, light, sound, water, and everyday science through playful discovery activities. Thirty real games — every one played on its own science illustration, with spoken instructions and a printable worksheet twin in the Science worksheet library.

Predictions to make, insects to count, magnets to test, habitats to match and one graduation lab — every question spoken aloud, every answer a picture.

Meet the adventures ↓Science is best in short, curious sittings.
PLAY · THE 30 SCIENCE ADVENTURES

Thirty science adventures.

Start anywhere curiosity points. The shelves run in a gentle order — grow first, graduate last — but every game stands alone. Each adventure twins with a printable worksheet at /worksheets/science/.

Seeds, butterflies and the water cycle — number the steps of how things grow and travel.

All 30 adventures are playable and printed today — Class 31 is complete, every game audited against its own artwork before it shipped.

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

Science play at the kitchen table.

Drop a spoon and a cork in the bath (04). Melt an ice cube on the windowsill (15). Raid the recycling with a magnet (11, 21). Grow a bean in a jam jar (01, 18). Blow a dandelion and watch the seeds fly (22). Every game here has a real experiment hiding inside it — the picture is the invitation.

A NOTE FROM THE PRINCIPAL

For the grown-ups.

Early science is predicting, testing and talking — never a quiz. Every game here asks your child to commit to a guess first, and every miss brings a friendly explanation instead of a penalty. The say-lines are written so YOU can steal them for bath time and walks.

The worksheets are the paper twins — the same experiments with room to predict, circle and draw. Browse the science worksheets and print the adventure your child loved. Playing games never marks a class complete; only real game finishes do, and only for the child chosen in My Classroom.
